title: Compatibility Hub & Upgrade Assistant for Image + Driver Lifecycles
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Problem: Upgrades to container images and GPU driver stacks are a frequent source of regressions for Redwood inference nodes. We currently depend on manual checks, ad-hoc SBOM comparisons, and single-matrix test runs that do not scale across LTS channels and variant kernels. This ticket implements a Compatibility Hub service and an Upgrade Assistant CLI that together: (1) produce machine-readable compatibility matrices linking image tags, SBOM digests, kernel/driver versions, and runtime artifacts; (2) run delta-SBOM diffs and vulnerability gating; (3) automate preflight checks for canary clusters and can compute safe rollout gates based on historical latency/error regressions; (4) generate signed upgrade manifests and automated rollback criteria for Dedicated and Private deployments. Scope excludes driver installer packaging; it focuses on metadata generation, compatibility verification pipelines, and rollout orchestration hooks for the Console and CI pipelines.
acceptance_criteria: Compatibility Hub API exposes a /compatibility/v1/matrix endpoint returning mapping of image:tag -> {sbom_digest, cuda_version, driver_build, kernel_compatibility_tags, known-good-test-set}
Upgrade Assistant CLI can ingest a target image tag and output a preflight report (delta-SBOM, CVE summary, driver mismatch warnings, suggested canary fraction and baseline tests)
CI pipeline integration: merge to runtime main triggers a compatibility snapshot job that produces a signed manifest artifact stored in the artifact registry
Rollout gate decision logic implemented as a pluggable evaluator: gates evaluate SLO delta, error-rate, and token-latency regressions; Console can visualize gate status per rollout
Automated rollback trigger defined: if canary latency p95 increases by >20% or error-rate doubles within 30 minutes, rollback automation initiates within the orchestration layer
SBOM diff tooling shows file-level delta and flags new binaries with no prior provenance; false-positive rate minimized by heuristics
Documentation and runbook added: upgrade-runbook.md linked in links field and a Console wiki page with instructions for DevOps and SREs
migration_steps: 1) Add a compatibility snapshot stage to existing runtime CI (jenkins/runtime-compat-snapshot) that emits SBOMs and driver fingerprints
2) Backfill compatibility Hub with last three months of published images and SBOMs to seed the matrix
3) Deploy Compatibility Hub behind internal API gateway and register schema with the service catalog
4) Release Upgrade Assistant CLI v0.1 as a github release and publish binary to internal bucket
5) Wire Console rollout UI to query Hub for suggested gates and to display preflight reports
6) Run two staged upgrades in a non-prod Dedicated cluster validating automated gates and rollback flows
7) Monitor and iterate for two cycles; once stable, enable for limited production cohorts before org-wide rollout
rollout_plan: Canary phase: 1% traffic in dedicated canary pool; run baseline workload for 4 hours with synthetic queries and a seeded prompt set
Confidence gates: compute p95 latency regression, request error-rate delta, model output divergence score (via eval harness). All must pass configured thresholds
Incremental ramp: 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 100% with gate checks at each step and a minimum observation window (30m, 1h, 2h respectively)
Fallback policy: automatic fallback to last-known-good image for the canary pool and alert SRE when gate fails during ramp
LTS channel promotion: after 2 successful full-production ramps separated by 7 days with no SLO regression, mark image as candidate for LTS channel and trigger security sign-off
test_plan: Unit: compatibility Hub schema validation, SBOM digest normalization, driver fingerprint parser
Integration: CI snapshot job writes signed manifest that the Hub ingests; validate round-trip
E2E: Upgrade Assistant preflight against staging cluster simulating incompatible driver reported and exercise automatic rollback path
Chaos: randomly inject 5% kernel OOMs and ensure rollback and alerting behave as expected
Performance: ensure compatibility Hub API returns matrix queries < 200ms P95 under typical load
risks: False positives from SBOM diffs can block safe upgrades; need tuned heuristics to avoid unnecessary rollbacks
Driver/kernel compatibility is hardware and distro dependent; risk of incomplete matrix for rare instance types
Signed manifests add operational complexity; key management mistakes could block upgrades
Performance overhead if compatibility checks run synchronously in the hot path of CI merges
monitoring: Create a 'compat-hub' grafana dashboard: snapshot job success rate, Hub API latency, manifest sign/ingest times
Console rollout dashboard: per-rollout gate status, canary metric deltas, auto-rollback events
Alerting: pager on manifest ingestion failure and on rollback-triggered incidents
Audit logs: every upgrade assistant preflight and manifest application must be logged with user and nonce
